fields.Resumption qualification(s):
What should I know about vaccination with the AstraZeneca vaccine?
People born in 1960 or earlier can safely continue to be injected with AstraZeneca. People born in 1961 or later will receive a different vaccine. The cabinet is thus following the advice of the Health Council . He argues that this can be done safely because the risk of health damage from corona in people over 60 is much greater than the risk of the reported very rare side effects of severe thrombosis with a low platelet count. To date, the side effects are mainly seen in people born in 1961 or later.

On Friday afternoon, April 2, 2021, vaccination with AstraZeneca of people born in 1961 or later was stopped as a precaution. Injecting continued in people born in 1960 or earlier.

fields.Resumption qualification(s):
AstraZeneca vaccine will not be used in women under 60 years of age with an increased risk of thrombosis and / or a history of thrombocytopenia. This was announced at a briefing by the Minister of Health Prof. Dr. Kostadin Angelov. The topic was discussed earlier today at a meeting of the National Vaccination Headquarters. The decisions of the Headquarters are as follows:

AstraZeneca vaccine should not be used in women under 60 years of age with an increased risk of thrombosis and / or a history of thrombocytopenia.
All subjects who received the first dose of AstraZeneca vaccine and did not experience any serious side effects can be immunized with a second dose of the same vaccine.
Individuals who have been vaccinated with the first dose of AstraZeneca and do not wish to receive a second dose of the same vaccine may receive a dose of Pfizer / BioNTech no earlier than 84 days after the first dose of AstraZeneca. The immunization is then considered complete.
In individuals with COVID-19 after administration of the first dose of vaccines with a two-dose immunization schedule, the second dose of vaccine should be given no earlier than 6 months after laboratory confirmation of the diagnosis.
COVID-19 survivors may be vaccinated with a full immunization schedule no earlier than 3 months after laboratory confirmation of the diagnosis.

 . Due to the increased risk observed in younger individuals, and the lower risk and higher bene t ratio of the above 60 years, the AstraZeneca vaccine will be offered to adults above the age of 60 years.
 . For adults who are below the age of 60 years, who have not yet received their  rst dose of AstraZeneca vaccine, they will not routinely be offered the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. Subject to availability, adults aged under 60 years will be offered another vaccine such as the Sinopharm vaccine.
 . The AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine can be used in adults aged under 60 years where the bene ts are likely to outweigh the risks for that individual and the person has made an informed consent based on an understanding of the risks and bene ts, and as well as has personally requested the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine.
8. To date, there are no reports of rare clotting/low platelets events following receipt of the second dose of the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. Therefore, for individuals who have received a  rst dose of the AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine should continue to receive a second dose of AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, irrespective of age. The second dose is important for longer lasting protection against COVID-19.
